metadata.title: The application of machine learning approaches in international large-scale educational assessments: A scoping review

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This scoping review does not conduct original student-level analyses of ILSA microdata; instead, it synthesizes 57 included empirical studies. Because no single assessment dataset (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS) is analyzed directly here, there is no study-specific sampling frame, weight application, or replicate-weight procedure to document. In the included studies, analysts would typically use the ILSA complex survey design weights (and replicate weights when available) to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors. However, this review focuses on mapping machine-learning approaches and research questions rather than re-estimating outcomes, so weighting variables are not extracted or applied at the review level.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this paper is a scoping review that does not estimate cognitive achievement outcomes from ILSA microdata. Instead, it summarizes characteristics of previously published empirical studies (e.g., which machine-learning methods were used and what research questions were addressed). Missing-data handling is not reported because no original dataset is analyzed in this review; therefore, there is no missingness mechanism or imputation/deletion strategy implemented by the authors on an ILSA dataset.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Not applicable for an original ILSA microdata analysis. The review identifies studies via database searches (Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO, ERIC) up to December 31, 2025, removes duplicates, screens abstracts, applies eligibility exclusions (non-quantitative designs, no machine learning, no international large-scale assessment data), and then includes 57 articles after full-text screening and supplementary citation searching.

data.outcome_summary: This scoping review synthesizes 57 peer-reviewed empirical studies that applied supervised machine learning to data from international large-scale educational assessments. Across the included studies, the review reports that the most frequently used machine-learning approaches were Random Forests (N=38), boosting algorithms (N=24), and Support Vector Machines (N=23), and that machine learning was used mainly for feature selection/importance analysis (N=54), comparative subgroup analyses (N=16), and model benchmarking for predictive accuracy (N=16). The review also summarizes theoretical frameworks used in the included studies (e.g., socio-ecological theory, PPCT, opportunity-propensity) and highlights strengths such as handling high-dimensional predictors and non-linear relationships. Because this is not an original empirical analysis, no single assessment cycle, country sample, or predictive performance metric is re-estimated here; consequently, limitations relate to the review’s descriptive mapping rather than to model evaluation validity.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a scoping review rather than an empirical ML study using a specific ILSA microdataset. As a result, there is no original student sample, no country-level analytic Ns, no survey-weight application, no plausible-values generation, and no missing-data handling strategy implemented by the authors on a shared dataset. The review therefore cannot provide dataset-specific predictive metrics (e.g., RMSE/AUC) or target-variable performance; it only reports frequencies and qualitative synthesis of methods and research questions across included studies.
